notes: scan054.N1: The author asks whether 21) d) should be strengthened to (24): every pair i,j has an infimum and its indexed piece is the intersection X_i cap X_j. A circle/cone example motivates hesitation. The lower paragraph introduces I_x and states the existence of a least containing index, summarized in (25). The final line begins a further construction and is left incomplete on this leaf.

scan054.N2: The phrase l'ens de ces I has a clearly capital I with both serifs. This can be an apparent authorial case slip for the individual indices i, but the capital is retained. It is not silently replaced by the lower-case i that would fit the grammar.

scan054.N3: Targeted conditional proof of the least-index assertion: let I_x be a finite nonempty downward-filtered subset of a poset, with members a_1,...,a_n. Start b_1=a_1. Successively choose b_k in I_x below b_{k-1} and a_k. Then b_n lies below every member of I_x, so it is a least element; antisymmetry gives uniqueness. This uses finite nonemptiness and downward filtering, not a global binary-meet axiom. This page asserts finiteness and filtering and cites (1' a) and (21 d); nonemptiness depends on the covering setup and was treated as an assumption in this isolated check.

scan054.N4: The written A cap B = {a} union {b} cannot describe two distinct disjoint strata literally. It is consistent with two closed arcs, or closures/pieces indexed by A and B, meeting at their endpoints. The text is not repaired to add closure bars or to rename the pieces. The mathematical discussion below is explicitly conditional on that closed-piece interpretation.

scan054.N5: Targeted topological check: for two closed arcs with intersection {a,b}, their full cones have intersection the cone on {a,b}, namely two rays/segments joined at the common apex. That intersection is path connected because every point can be joined to the apex. Deleting the apex, or passing to the corresponding link, leaves two components. Thus the author's disconnected-intersection remark requires a punctured-local or link qualification if the pieces are these cones. The check does not decide the handwritten 0/o label or alter the sentence.

scan054.N6: A conditional five-piece model still supports the distinction the question is making. Order the five indices as vertex < a,b < A,B, where a and b are incomparable and each is below both A and B. The pointwise containing-index sets have least elements: vertex at the apex, a or b on a nonzero boundary ray, and A or B in the two interiors. Yet the common lower bounds of A and B are vertex,a,b, with no greatest one. Hence this closed-piece model is locally finite and pointwise downward filtered but fails the global meet requirement of (24), whether or not the full cone intersection is called disconnected.

scan054.N7: The short live form before au point de vue local has a definite overbar. A reduced m is the preferred but uncertain letter reading, with overlined vu retained as an alternative. Même is a possible expansion only; neither it nor H's ne serait-ce is supplied as running text.

scan054.N8: All four apex labels are round 0/o forms: d'origine, locale en, dont parentheses, and below the drawn apex. The local-en form is retraced, but the extra strokes do not settle the alphabet or reveal a readable cancelled character. All four retain 0|o, with separate physical-place rows. These are C certainty additions only; the tentative preferred 0 reading differs from H's o.

scan054.N9: The diagram is drawn from its ink, with the heavier A arc, lighter B arc, parallel lower A trace, short a-side stub, interrupted rays and left boundary stopping short of the ring. The small tick right of a is one of the broken-line strokes, not an a-prime label. No missing continuous generators are supplied merely to make an ideal cone.

scan054.N10: Def in (24) is unaccented and above the equality. The two l'ens forms and nb have no supplied stops. Question is underlined without a period. The explicit line-end split l'élimi- / ner is retained, while the lexical reading remains l'éliminer. The two long dashes use the edition's normal dash encoding.

scan054.N11: The four cancelled passages are d'un sommet (uncertain reading), n'est pas, et, and tel que. Il, ne me, the des below the lower insertion leader, and the commas before et and after tel que remain live. The raised cercles attaches after des; the lower l'ens I_x subset I attaches between considérons and the live des.

scan054.N12: The pale bottom-left 53 is foliation in another hand. No dark authorial page numeral appears at the head. H's note and drawing-description prose are editorial descriptions, not additional handwritten manuscript text; they are excluded from the source transcription.

scan054.N13: The whole page and both native halves were each inspected once, with every line compared against C and H. All 18 saved crops were inspected. r06 was extended upward while the place remained open to include the full d'origine ascender; the final original box is [921,880,1608,1002]. Reading counts include 23 main rows, including display rows and foliation; raised insertions and drawing labels were separately inventoried and inspected. No other page source or reader report was opened, and TeX was not compiled.

scan054.N14. Blind adjudication preserves the actual plural des cercles, disconnexe, montrera, four matching 0/o labels and the detailed drawing. The accent of cone/cône is uncertain, with the unaccented form preferred. The crossed d-un sommet now records d-origine as another doubtful proposal, and n-est pas is explicitly qualified because its middle lies under the strike. The small a/0 in the reference remains unresolved. These qualifications do not alter the conditional mathematical checks above.

checks.outcome: Finite nonempty downward-filtered poset subsets have a unique least member by successive pairwise lower bounds. Nonemptiness and the surrounding covering setup are explicit assumptions of this isolated check; no global meet hypothesis is needed.

For the closed-arc cone model, the full intersection is two rays joined at the apex and is connected; its punctured version or link has two components. This qualifies, rather than silently rewrites, the author's disconnected-intersection statement.

In the five-index model vertex < a,b < A,B, the pointwise filters have the listed least members, while A and B have the incomparable maximal lower bounds a,b. Thus global pairwise infima are not forced in this conditional closed-piece model.
